originalTitle: Seven Ethiopian rebel groups form new alliance
title: Big News from Ethiopia! Groups Join Hands!
content:
Hi everyone! It's your friendly news reporter, **Rory the Reporter**! I bring you exciting news from a very special country in Africa called Ethiopia. It's a land of sunshine, amazing history, and wonderful people, just like you! Today, we're talking about some big groups of people in Ethiopia. For a long, long time, these groups had their own ideas about how things should be. Now, something really interesting has happened! They've decided to team up, just like you and your friends might team up to play a game or build a sandcastle!

Hello from Ethiopia!

Imagine a country with lots of different mountains, rivers, and tasty food like injera. That's Ethiopia! It's a very old and beautiful country. Many different people live there, and they speak many different languages. **Did you know?** Ethiopia is famous for being the birthplace of coffee! So next time an adult drinks coffee, you can tell them it probably came from Ethiopia many, many years ago! Think of Ethiopia as a really big playground. In this big playground, there are lots of different neighborhoods. In these neighborhoods, people have ideas about how to make things even better. Sometimes, they might not agree with everything that is happening.

What is Happening?

For many years, there were different groups of people in Ethiopia. Each group wanted to see changes in their part of the country. They wanted things to be different, maybe better roads, better schools, or just for their voices to be heard more clearly. These groups lived in places where many, many people live. These are called "populous regions." Imagine your town, but much, much bigger, with millions of people! That's a populous region. **Did you know?** Ethiopia is home to some amazing animals like the Gelada Baboon! They are like monkeys with fluffy hair! These groups used to work by themselves. They were like many small teams, each trying to win their own game. But now, they have a new idea. They decided to join up and become one really, really big team!

Making a Super Team!

This is the big news! Seven different groups have said, "Hey! Let's work together!" This is like seven small puzzle pieces fitting together to make one big picture. When they work together, they can be much stronger. Think about it this way: If you want to move a very big toy, it's hard to do by yourself, right? But if you ask six of your friends to help, it becomes super easy! That's exactly what these groups are doing. **Did you know?** The capital city of Ethiopia is called Addis Ababa. It means 'New Flower'! They have formed a new "alliance." An alliance just means a special agreement to work together. It's like making a promise to be on the same team and help each other. They believe that by joining up, their voices will be much louder, and they can make bigger changes.

Why Groups Want Change

Sometimes, people in different parts of a country feel like they are not being listened to. They might want things to be fairer for everyone. Maybe they want better hospitals for when people get sick, or more jobs for grown-ups so families can be happy. These groups are saying, "We want things to be better for all the people in our communities!" They want to see good things happen for their friends, their families, and their neighbors. **Did you know?** Ethiopia is one of the oldest countries in the world! Its history goes back thousands of years, even before many other countries were formed. It's like when you have an idea for a fun game, but no one listens to you. But if all your friends have the same idea and you all say it together, suddenly everyone listens! That's the power of working together.

Working Together is Stronger

The leaders of these groups have said that they will now "work together." This means they will share their ideas, plan things together, and help each other reach their goals. They are no longer just thinking about their own small group, but about the bigger team. It's like building a strong bridge. If each person tries to build their own tiny piece of the bridge, it won't be very strong. But if everyone works together, using the same plan, they can build a wonderful, strong bridge for everyone to use. **Did you know?** Ethiopia has many ancient churches carved right out of rock! They are very, very old and look amazing. This new big team wants to bring peace and fairness to their country. They want to make sure everyone has a chance to live a good life. They are hoping that by being united, they can make a positive difference for all the children and grown-ups in Ethiopia.

Hopes for a Happy Future

When groups come together like this, it often brings a lot of hope. Hope means wishing for good things to happen, and believing that they can happen. The people of Ethiopia, especially the children, want to live in a peaceful and happy country. This new big team is a step towards that hope. They want to talk about the changes they wish to see. They want to make sure that everyone's voice is heard, from the smallest child to the oldest grandparent. **Did you know?** Ethiopia has more than 80 different languages! Imagine how many ways people can say 'hello'! So, this is very important news. It shows how people can decide to put their differences aside and work as one big family to make their country a better place. It's all about teamwork, listening, and hoping for a bright, bright future for everyone in Ethiopia! What a wonderful lesson in coming together!
summary: Seven groups in Ethiopia who wanted changes have now decided to work together as one big team to make their country a better place for everyone.
whyMatters: This is important because when groups work together, their voices become stronger, and they can make bigger and better changes for peace and fairness in their country, like building better schools or roads for everyone.

originalTitle: Two charged with woman's murder as South Africa police investigate eight other body finds
title: Our Police Heroes Are Keeping Us Safe!
content:
Hi everyone! It's your friendly reporter here, bringing you news from our amazing continent, Africa! Today, we're talking about something very important: staying safe and how our wonderful police officers help us every single day. They are like super helpers in our towns and cities!

Big News from Our Community!

Sometimes, people in our community feel worried. That's okay! Grown-ups feel worried too, and sometimes kids do. It's important to remember that we have people who care about us very much. Our police officers are some of these caring people. They work hard to make sure everyone is safe. Recently, in a place near a big city called Johannesburg in South Africa, some people were very worried. Some people went missing, and their families missed them so much. When someone goes missing, it means they are not where they usually are, and people can't find them. The police heard about this. And what did they do? They got straight to work! Police officers are like super-detectives. They are very clever at looking for clues and trying to find people. They started a big search. They wanted to help the families and find out what happened.

How Our Police Heroes Work

Our police officers have a very important job. They help keep the peace. This means they make sure everyone follows the rules. Rules help us live together happily and safely. When someone breaks a rule, the police help fix it. **Did you know?** The police wear special uniforms so you can always spot them! Their uniforms might be blue or sometimes khaki, depending on where you are in Africa. When something important happens, like someone going missing, the police start something called an 'investigation.' This is like solving a big puzzle! They look for clues, they ask questions, and they try to put all the pieces together. It's a bit like when you try to find your favourite toy after it gets lost – you look everywhere, right? In this story near Johannesburg, the police have been working extra, extra hard. They found some important clues. And because they are so good at their jobs, they have even arrested some people. 'Arrested' means they have asked some grown-ups to come with them to the police station. These grown-ups might know something important about what happened. The police want to talk to these people. They want to understand everything. This helps them keep everyone safe in the future. It's like when your teacher finds out why someone is sad – they talk to everyone to make things better.

Staying Super Safe!

It's super important for all of us, especially you brave kids, to know how to stay safe. Here are some simple rules to remember: **1. Always tell a grown-up where you are going.** Whether it's to your friend's house or just outside to play, let an adult know. This is very important! **2. Know your safe grown-ups.** These are people you trust, like your parents, grandparents, teachers, or a trusted neighbour. If you ever feel scared or lost, you can go to one of them. **3. Don't talk to strangers.** If someone you don't know tries to talk to you, or asks you to go somewhere with them, always say 'NO!' and run straight to a grown-up you trust. Shout loudly if you need to! **Did you know?** Your voice is a powerful tool! If you ever feel unsafe, use your voice to shout for help! **4. If you see something strange, tell an adult.** Maybe you see something that doesn't look right, or someone acting strangely. It's okay to tell a grown-up. They can help decide what to do.

Our Community Cares!

Our communities are like big families. Everyone looks out for each other. When police are working hard, our neighbors are also helping. They share information and make sure their friends and family are okay. **Did you know?** In many parts of Africa, people live in close communities where neighbors often help each other with daily tasks, like sharing food or looking after children. It's called 'ubuntu' in some places, which means 'I am because we are' – we are all connected! When everyone works together, our towns and villages become much safer places. We all have a part to play, even you! By being kind, looking out for your friends, and telling grown-ups when you need help, you are helping too.

The Police Are Always There to Help

It's good to remember that our police officers are always there to help. They want to keep everyone safe. If you ever feel lost, scared, or need help, you can look for a police officer. They are friendly people who are trained to assist you. It can be scary when big news happens, but it's important to remember that there are many people working hard to make things better. The police in South Africa are working very hard on this case. They want to make sure everyone is safe and that justice is done. Justice means making things fair and right. When something wrong happens, the police and other grown-ups work to make sure things are made right again. This helps everyone feel better and safer.

Let's Be Kind and Safe!

So, my dear friends, remember to always be kind to each other. Look out for your friends and family. And know that our amazing police heroes are always on duty, keeping an eye out for all of us. Let's say a big thank you to all the police officers in South Africa and all over Africa who work so hard to keep our homes and communities safe. You are true heroes!
summary: Our amazing police officers in South Africa are working hard to keep everyone safe, investigating when people go missing, and reminding us all to follow safety rules and look out for each other in our kind communities.
whyMatters: This is important because it reminds us that police are here to help keep us safe, and that we can all work together in our communities to look after each other and make sure everyone feels protected.

originalTitle: Former ‘death squad’ leader appears in military trial in The Gambia
title: A Big Day for Rules in The Gambia!
content:
Hello, my super little friends! Are you ready to hear a cool story from Africa? Today, we're flying over to a beautiful country called The Gambia. It's a sunny place with friendly people and lots of amazing animals! We're going to talk about something important happening there – it's all about rules and why they keep everyone safe and fair.

What is Happening in The Gambia?

Imagine you have rules at home and at school, right? Like, don't run in the hallway, or always say please and thank you. Well, countries also have rules, and even soldiers who protect the country have special rules they must follow. Something very important is happening in The Gambia right now. A soldier named Sanna Manjang is in a special court. It's called a military trial. Did you know? The Gambia is the smallest country on mainland Africa! It's shaped like a thin stick around a river!

Who is Sanna Manjang?

Sanna Manjang was once a soldier for The Gambia. Soldiers are important people because they help keep the country safe. They wear uniforms and learn how to protect everyone. Sanna Manjang was part of a special group under the old leader of The Gambia. Now, he is in a special court because of something that happened a few years ago.

What is a Military Trial?

Think of a military trial like a special school court, but just for soldiers! If a student breaks a rule at school, they might talk to the principal or a teacher. In the army, if a soldier breaks a very important rule, they go to a military trial. There are special judges who are also soldiers, and they listen very carefully to what happened. They make sure everything is fair and that the rules are followed. It's a serious place where people talk about truth and rules. Everyone gets a chance to tell their side of the story. The judges then decide what is fair and what should happen next. Did you know? Soldiers train very hard to be strong and smart. They learn many skills, like how to help people in emergencies!

What Rule Did He Break?

Sanna Manjang is in this special court because he left his job as a soldier without telling anyone or getting permission. This is called 'deserting' the army. Imagine if you decided to just leave school in the middle of the day without telling your teacher or your parents! That would not be allowed, right? It's the same for soldiers. When you are a soldier, you promise to stay and protect your country. Leaving your post without permission is a very big rule to break in the army. Soldiers have important jobs to do, and if they leave suddenly, it can be dangerous for others and for the country. So, the court needs to understand why he left and make sure the rules are kept.

When Did This Happen?

This story happened a few years ago, in 2017. That was a very big and important year for The Gambia! Before 2017, The Gambia had the same leader for 20 whole years! That's a very long time – probably longer than you've been alive! After 20 years, that old leader left, and The Gambia got a new leader. It was a time of big change and new beginnings for the country. Many people were very happy and hoped for a better future where everyone followed the rules and treated each other kindly. Sanna Manjang left the army around the time of these big changes. Did you know? The capital city of The Gambia is Banjul! It's a busy place right next to the Atlantic Ocean!

Why is Following Rules Important?

Rules are super important for everyone! They help us know what is safe to do and what is not. They help us treat each other fairly and with respect. Imagine if there were no rules at all – it might be very messy and confusing! For an army, rules are even more important. They make sure all the soldiers work together like a team and keep their country safe. This court case shows that everyone, no matter who they are or what job they do, has to follow the rules. It means that The Gambia wants to be a country where justice is fair for everyone.

What Happens Next?

The judges at the military trial will listen to all the stories and look at all the facts. They will think very carefully about the rules and what is fair. After listening to everything, they will decide what should happen. This process helps The Gambia move forward, making sure everyone feels safe and that the rules are important. We hope for fairness and peace for all the wonderful people in The Gambia. And remember, friends, following rules helps make the world a better, safer, and happier place for everyone!
summary: A soldier named Sanna Manjang is in a special court in The Gambia because he left the army without permission in 2017, after the country got a new leader.
whyMatters: This is important because it shows that everyone, even soldiers, must follow the rules to keep a country fair and safe for everyone.
